pr_title: driver: adc: stm32: support dma for devices without dmamux
pr_body:
Previously the STM32 DMA driver was dependent on a very specific
name for the DMA in the DTS. This hidden requirement has caused
a bit of confusion. This commit changes the driver to instead
always use the first DMA listed in the ADC node's dma property.

Also, updates the dma code in the ADC driver to support the STM32L4 (and likely more other mcus)

Fixes: #65387
pr_comments:
> My understanding is that we're extending ADC DMA support to 'non dmamux' compatible series.

Yes, that's the goal.

> Would you mind adding at least target of this kind to tests/drivers/adc/adc_dma ?

I would like to, but it doesn't seem to work fully just yet. I found a possible problem which I mentioned on the Discord in the `#adc` channel. If I can verify that it does work I will add the test.

My plan was to merge this PR first as it works standalone IMO. It doesn't imply functionality without a dmamux. And once functionality is verified create a new PR with test (and maybe a sample) that has the title something explicit like "support non dmamux mcus".

Would you prefer I put everything into one PR?

---
**Update:** Just added a test into this PR as well.

@erwango I've added tests for the `nucleo_l476rg`. I can't run it though as I don't have this board. The person who brought up this issue initially said they might get time to run it on their hardware later this week.

issue_context.title: ADC via DMA on STM32:  DMA device is null and `dma_config()` leads to Instruction Address Violation
comments:
Hi @doodek! We appreciate you submitting your first issue for our open-source project. 🌟

Even though I'm a bot, I can assure you that the whole community is genuinely grateful for your time and effort. 🤖💙

A developer who has this same issue also mentioned that they the following warning. This would mean that `CONFIG_ADC_STM32_DMA=y` as expected, but somehow the dma `struct stream` is never filled. This would explain the `dma.dev_data` being `NULL`, and the callback never used.
```
z-workspace/zephyr/drivers/adc/adc_stm32.c:713:13: warning: 'dma_callback' defined but not used [-Wunused-function]
  713 | static void dma_callback(const struct device *dev, void *user_data,
      |             ^~~~~~~~~~~~
[142/142] Linking C executable zephyr/zephyr.elf
```
This will only happen if this `DT_INST_DMAS_HAS_NAME` is false, which would result in an `EMPTY`. (Which is an odd silent failure to have. It should be better). _(Update: the silent ignoring is for other ADC instances which do not have dmas defined)_
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/bc08e801c6b1416dcbbc679f5e25f801d438a531/drivers/adc/adc_stm32.c#L1553-L1556

Which is most likely caused by the driver currently requiring a _dmamux_ to function, and not _any_ dma.
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/bc08e801c6b1416dcbbc679f5e25f801d438a531/drivers/adc/adc_stm32.c#L1604-L1609

Of the top of my head I'm not sure how this should be fixed.

That's an interesting insight! Before I have a deeper look into that, I would like to say that while this issue example is from F4 microcontroller without DMAMUX, I had the same problem on a STM32G0 with DMAMUX, used as in the documentation:
`dmas = <&dmamux1 .... >;`

> That's an interesting insight! Before I have a deeper look into that, I would like to say that while this issue example is from F4 microcontroller without DMAMUX, I had the same problem on a STM32G0 with DMAMUX, used as in the documentation: `dmas = <&dmamux1 .... >;`

Digging a little deeper, I don't think that's actually the limitation. Instead the DTS **_has_** to name the dma `dmamux`, regardless of if it's actually an dmamux or not. Otherwise it will silently be ignored, and then you'll see the behaviour you saw which explained in my previous comment. So you would need:

```dts
dma-names="dmamux";
```

Kind of a silly current limitation. Thinking of creating a PR to rename it to simply `dma`. Other drivers name it useful names like `tx` and `rx`, but these don't make sense in this case. @erwango any thoughts on this?

Also, there should be a mechanism to prevent the silent ignoring, but working that into the macro magic is not that easy. Hit my head against it now for a bit. Will see if I can maybe come up with a solution.

review_comments:
A quick look through the LL shows that the macro `LL_ADC_REG_DMA_TRANSFER_LIMITED` does not exist for F1 and F37x.
For those, the choice is between `LL_ADC_REG_DMA_TRANSFER_NONE` or `LL_ADC_REG_DMA_TRANSFER_UNLIMITED`.
A `#elif DT_HAS_COMPAT_STATUS_OKAY(st_stm32f1_adc)` should be added for these cases. What we do inside is up to you: unlimited seems to imply a circular buffer, which may be hard to add, so maybe we can just not support this case for now and return an error.

I would prefer to error as "not supported", as I do not have hardware or time to investigate all potential edge cases at the moment. And my idea was that my code as-is doesn't compile then it already implies "not supported", but I can make this explicit.
